title: Canonical strict derived-limit comparison for exact product-preserving module functors
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites with sheaves of commutative rings $R,S$, and put $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ and $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Mod}(S)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in both categories are exact. Let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and exact and assume its canonical countable-product comparison $\phi:F(\prod_nM_n)\to\prod_nF(M_n)$, characterized by $\mathrm{pr}_n\phi=F(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, is an isomorphism for every family. Write $F_D$ for its termwise derived functor [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], and $F^{\operatorname{Tow}}_D$ for termwise application to complexes of strict towers [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. Let $L_{\mathcal A},L_{\mathcal B}$ be total right derived inverse limit [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit].

There is a natural isomorphism
$$\lambda_M:F_D L_{\mathcal A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{\mathcal B}F^{\operatorname{Tow}}_D M.$$
It is the following specified comparison. For a strict tower complex $M$ with transition shift $s$, put $P_M=\prod_nM_n$ termwise and let $H_M^q=P_M^q\oplus P_M^{q-1}$ with differential $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. Use the normalized natural Roos isomorphism of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], in these signed coordinates, to write $\theta_M:L_{\mathcal A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}H_M$; its K-injective normalization is $z\mapsto(\iota z,0)$. If $\kappa_M:F_DH_M\to H_{FM}$ is the map $\phi$ on both summands, then
$$\lambda_M=\theta_{FM}^{-1}\kappa_M F_D(\theta_M).$$
This equals the comparison obtained by preserving the ordinary inverse limit and then resolving the image tower: for $M\to I$ K-injective and $F I\to J$ a K-injective target resolution, it is represented by $F\lim I\cong\lim F I\to\lim J$ and the inverse of the derived image of $FM\to FI$. It is independent of those resolutions. For the specified Roos triangles, with first maps $p,p'$ and connecting maps $\delta,\delta'$, and the shift comparison $\xi$, it satisfies
$$p'\lambda_M=\phi F_D(p),\qquad\lambda_M[1]\xi F_D(\delta)=\delta'\phi.$$
For every complex $C$ and strict augmentation $\gamma:\Delta C\to M$, it carries $F_D$ of the canonical derived map $C\to L_{\mathcal A}M$ induced by $\gamma$ to the canonical derived map $F_DC\to L_{\mathcal B}FM$ induced by $F\gamma$. Here $\Delta C$ is the constant tower; both maps are those of the normalized Roos comparison, equivalently of the constant-tower/derived-limit adjunction.

proof.text: By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], exact additive $F$ acts termwise on the derived categories. The same applies on strict towers: exactness there is levelwise by [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-products-core], the two exact-countable-product hypotheses identify derived products with termwise products. Thus the degreewise isomorphism $\phi:F(P_M)\to P_{FM}$ represents the canonical derived product comparison: its $n$-th projection is $F(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, which characterizes that comparison. This proves the needed preservation of derived countable products without a new lemma.

source.place: Tags 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor) and 07KC (lemma-products); levelwise tower exactness: homology.tex Tag 02MZ

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] for both module categories. In the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], write an element of $\operatorname{Cone}(1-s)[-1]^q$ as $(u,v)\in P_M^{q-1}\oplus P_M^q$. The coordinate change $(u,v)\mapsto(v,-u)$ gives $H_M^q=P_M^q\oplus P_M^{q-1}$ and $d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy)$. It sends the normalized inclusion of the inverse limit to $z\mapsto(\iota z,0)$. Invert the cited natural $\rho$ in these coordinates to obtain $\theta_M:L_{\mathcal A}M\xrightarrow{\sim}H_M$, and likewise for $FM$. These are functorial on the derived categories of strict towers, not just on the evaluated diagrams.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), K-injective product-cone calculation; signed-coordinate refinement of the existing Roos node

proof.text: For each $n$, the $n$-th projection of $\phi F(s)$ and of $s'\phi$ is $F(t_n)F(\mathrm{pr}_{n+1})$. Product uniqueness gives $\phi F(s)=s'\phi$. Naturality of $\phi$ also gives $\phi F(d)=d\phi$, and additivity gives $\phi F(1-s)=(1-s')\phi$. Identify $F(P^q\oplus P^{q-1})$ with $F(P^q)\oplus F(P^{q-1})$ by its biproduct projections and inclusions. The block diagonal map with entries $\phi^q,\phi^{q-1}$ then intertwines the two displayed differential matrices, so defines a chain isomorphism $\kappa_M:F(H_M)\to H_{FM}$. Its inverse is the same block diagonal construction with $\phi^{-1}$.

source.place: Tag 07KC (lemma-products), product projections; direct calculation in the signed fiber model

proof.text: Set $\lambda_M=\theta_{FM}^{-1}\kappa_MF_D(\theta_M)$. Every factor is invertible. If $h:M\to N$ is a strict map of tower complexes, the product projection identities give $P(Fh)\phi_M=\phi_NF(P(h))$; the same identity on the two summands gives $H(Fh)\kappa_M=\kappa_NF(H(h))$. Together with the naturality supplied by [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] this proves naturality of $\lambda$. The Roos construction descends to the derived tower category by that same cited statement, and $F$ does so by Step 1. Naturality for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms follows by multiplying the naturality equation by their inverses, hence holds for every derived morphism.

The fiber projection is $p_H(x,y)=x$. Hence $p_{H'}\kappa=\phi F(p_H)$. In the cone convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the connecting map from the second product to $H[1]$ has zero first component and the fixed signed identity in the second component. Applying the block diagonal $\kappa[1]$ therefore gives the same map as first applying $\phi$ and then the target connecting map; additivity preserves its sign. The termwise shift comparison $\xi$ identifies the two shifted complexes (their differentials are both negated). Conjugating these two coordinate equations by the $\theta$'s of Step 2 yields exactly $p'\lambda_M=\phi F_D(p)$ and $\lambda_M[1]\xi F_D(\delta)=\delta'\phi$.

source.place: Cone/shift convention of the abstract derived-category node; explicit projection and signed-inclusion calculation

proof.text: The ordinary limit of a strict tower $T$ is the kernel of $1-s:P_T\to P_T$: a map to this kernel is exactly a family of compatible maps to the $T_n$. Applying exact $F$ preserves this kernel, and $\phi F(1-s)=(1-s')\phi$ identifies it with the kernel defining $\lim FT$. This gives a natural isomorphism $\beta_T:F\lim T\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim FT$, characterized by $\mathrm{pr}_n\beta_T=F(\mathrm{pr}_n)$. Apply this argument degreewise to complexes; the same projection identities make $\beta$ a chain isomorphism. No preservation of arbitrary infinite limits is being assumed.

source.place: Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), ordinary inverse limit; kernel description proved here

proof.text:
Apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the small tower site $\mathcal C\times\mathbf N$ with the ring pulled back from $\mathcal C$: the sheaf condition and module structure at each level identify its module sheaves with strict module towers. This supplies the injective-term resolutions below, and likewise for $\mathcal D$. First choose $q:M\to I$ and $r:FI\to J$ K-injective tower resolutions with injective terms, as in [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison]. Write $a_I:\lim I\to H_I$ and $a_J:\lim J\to H_J$ for the normalized inclusions. The cited statement makes both quasi-isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], $L_{\mathcal A}M$ is represented by $\lim I$ and $L_{\mathcal B}FI$ by $\lim J$. There is the literal chain-map identity
$$a_J(\lim r)\beta_I=H(r)\kappa_I F(a_I):F\lim I\longrightarrow H_J.$$
Indeed, the $n$-th first-product component of either side is $r_nF(\mathrm{pr}_n)$, and the shifted-product component is zero. The normalized formula for $\theta_{FI}$ is $H(r)^{-1}a_J$. Cancelling $H(r)$ in this identity therefore identifies $\lambda_I$ with $(\lim r)\beta_I$. Naturality for $q$ from Step 4 identifies $\lambda_M$ with this map followed by $(L_{\mathcal B}Fq)^{-1}$, exactly the stated resolution comparison. This argument never assumes that $FI$ is K-injective.

source.place: Tag 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok), normalized inclusions; strict-augmentation comparison calculated on both summands

proof.text:
The formula also holds for K-injective resolutions $I,J$ without degreewise injectivity. Choose further K-injective resolutions $a:I\to I^+$ and $b:J\to J^+$ with injective terms using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the small tower sites of Step 7. By [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], $a,b$ are homotopy equivalences. Thus $F(a)$ is a homotopy equivalence; the derived map $Q(FI^+)\to QJ^+$ given by $Q(br)Q(Fa)^{-1}$ is represented by a chain map $r^+:FI^+\to J^+$, and $r^+Fa$ is homotopic to $br$, by the same bijectivity into K-injectives. Additive $F$ and termwise $\lim$ preserve homotopies, and $\lim a,\lim b$ are homotopy equivalences. Naturality of $\beta$ gives
$$(\lim b)(\lim r)\beta_I\simeq(\lim r^+)\beta_{I^+}F(\lim a).$$
Transporting Step 7 through these isomorphisms proves its formula for the original $I,J$. Since that formula equals the already defined natural $\lambda$, its value is independent of every resolution and comparison choice.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective), bijectivity into K-injectives and homotopy equivalences; Tag 0941 normalization

proof.text: Let $\gamma:\Delta C\to M$ be a strict augmentation. By the final clause of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], its canonical derived map is represented in $H_M$ by $c\mapsto((\gamma_n(c))_n,0)$. After applying $F$, the $n$-th projection of the first component followed by $\phi$ is $F(\gamma_n)$, and the second component stays zero. Thus $\kappa_MF(\theta_M)$ carries $F$ of this map to the signed-fiber map of $F\gamma$. Applying $\theta_{FM}^{-1}$ and the cited augmentation clause gives precisely the asserted canonical map $F_DC\to L_{\mathcal B}FM$. This proves the augmentation equality, not just agreement of its evaluations.

Statement: unchanged and no weaker than what its citers use, which are Steps 6 and 11 of lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison and Steps 3 and 10 of thm-cbc-complete-proetale. They use the signed Roos model with lambda = theta^-1 kappa F(theta), the two triangle equations and the strict-augmentation clause. Coefficients are Mod(R) and Mod(S) on small sites, both with exact countable products. Step checks: Step 2's signs follow from the cone convention of def-weil-abstract-derived-category; changing (u,v) to (v,-u) gives d(x,y)=(dx,(1-s)x-dy), and the Roos inclusion (0,iota z) becomes (iota z,0). Steps 3 and 5 hold because kappa is block diagonal and F is additive. Step 7: I recomputed a_J(lim r)beta_I = H(r)kappa_I F(a_I) by components; the n-th product component is r_n F(pi_n) and the shifted component is 0. With theta_{FI} = H(r)^-1 a_J this gives lambda_I = (lim r)beta_I. Step 8: the argument for arbitrary K-injective resolutions uses only what the 070I node states (bijection into K-injectives, homotopy equivalences). Step 9: the augmentation clause gives (F gamma_n, 0). Applying resolution existence on the tower site matches Step 1 of lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit and Stacks 0941, which I read at sites-cohomology.tex lines 5067-5107; I also confirmed the cited tags 07KC and 070I in the tag table. Edge cases: F=id gives identities; zero transitions make both sides 0. With F = -⊗Q on Ab and the tower Z <-p- Z, (R^1 lim)⊗Q is nonzero while the image tower Q <-p- Q has Rlim = Q, so the product hypothesis is necessary. Duplicates: none in the DAG. lem-cbc-exact-functor-rlim is pro-etale and existence only; lem-pc-derived-functor-commutes-derived-limit has no canonical map; lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison is about direct images, not an exact functor.
